BackstoryDef.title: farm-fostered
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was raised on a moisture farm by an aunt and uncle who were not [PAWN_possessive] parents, and who never fully explained why. [PAWN_pronoun] did chores at dawn, argued about going to the academy, and spent every dusk staring at the horizon as if it owed [PAWN_objective] something.

BackstoryDef.title: raider-orphaned
BackstoryDef.description: Sand people came at night and by morning [PAWN_nameDef] had no family and one working rifle. The homesteads raised [PAWN_objective] in shifts after that, and every household taught the same two lessons: how to shoot, and how to keep watch while others sleep.

BackstoryDef.title: moisture baron
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] ran a homestead of thirty vaporators and defended every one of them from raiders, cartels and drought. [PAWN_pronoun] believes in early mornings, honest ledgers and minding one's own business, and has said no to stronger people than you.

BackstoryDef.title: homestead matron
BackstoryDef.description: Every farm within a day's ride knew [PAWN_nameDef]'s table. [PAWN_pronoun] fed harvest crews, set broken arms, kept the peace between quarrelling households, and asked the questions nobody else dared ask over dinner. A homestead is walls and water; [PAWN_pronoun] was what made it a home.

BackstoryDef.title: hermit of the wastes
BackstoryDef.description: The homesteaders called [PAWN_nameDef] a crazy old wizard and left [PAWN_objective] alone, which suited everyone. [PAWN_pronoun] lived past the dune sea, appeared when krayt dragons or raiders threatened the farms, and vanished again before anyone could ask where [PAWN_pronoun] learned to fight like that — or what [PAWN_pronoun] was watching over, all those years.

BackstoryDef.title: sun-sworn child
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was carried through [PAWN_possessive] first sandstorm strapped to a parent's back, and given to the Sun-Debt rites as soon as [PAWN_pronoun] could walk. The deep desert is not something [PAWN_pronoun] survives. It is something [PAWN_pronoun] belongs to.

BackstoryDef.title: krayt-watcher
BackstoryDef.description: Before [PAWN_nameDef] was old enough to carry a weapon, [PAWN_pronoun] was old enough to sit on a canyon rim and watch for the great beasts. [PAWN_pronoun] learned how sand moves when something is under it, and how much of courage is simply not running.

BackstoryDef.title: water-raider
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] rode with the fast bands that strike the settlements' cisterns and are gone before the dust settles. To outsiders it is theft. To the tribes it is repayment — the Sun-Debt collected from those who cage sacred water in machines. [PAWN_pronoun] carries more than [PAWN_possessive] share and never strikes the same place twice.

BackstoryDef.title: beast-bonded nomad
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was paired with a herd-beast in the old way: one animal, one rider, one life shared between them. [PAWN_pronoun] knows the deep desert's safe crossings the way settled people know their own hallways, and treats animals with a courtesy [PAWN_pronoun] does not always extend to people.

BackstoryDef.title: sun-debt cantor
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] keeps the tribe's oldest ledger: what the sun gives, what the living owe, and what must never be done to water. [PAWN_pronoun] sings the rites at wells and burials, speaks for the tribe at parley, and has argued more than one war chief out of a battle — and into a better one.

BackstoryDef.title: pyre-watcher
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] kept the season's first fires — the ones that scorch the Pyrelands bare so the rains after can feed the tribe. [PAWN_pronoun] learned to read a burn scar the way others read a face, and has never once flinched from what the flame reveals.

BackstoryDef.title: flame-reaper
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] is the tribe's warrior-hunter elite: the one sent to burn what does not belong, and to work the scorched ground after for whatever it gives up. [PAWN_pronoun] does not grieve a burning structure or a burning corpse — that grief belongs to people who have not yet understood what fire is for.

BackstoryDef.title: ash-speaker
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] walks the burn scars once the smoke clears and reads what regrew — who belongs, who does not, who has earned the tribe's water. It is a rare gift, and the tribe does not overrule it: [PAWN_pronoun] can ease an outsider's road into the fire-faith, or close it, with a word.
